introduction: On this sixth Sunday of Easter, Philip preaches in Samaria, and Peter and John lay hands on the new believers so that they receive the Holy Spirit. In the Gospel, Jesus promises to send another Advocate, the Spirit of truth, and says, I will not leave you orphans. Peter urges us to always be ready to give a reason for our hope. Let us open our hearts to the Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus has promised not to leave us orphans. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, filled with the Holy Spirit, she may bring the joy of the Gospel to every city. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those preparing for Confirmation: that they may receive the Spirit of truth with open hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For orphans and all who feel abandoned: that they may know the love of the Father. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are mocked or slandered for their faith: that they may answer with gentleness and reverence. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may always be ready to explain the hope that is in us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, your Son promised to send the Spirit of truth and not to leave us orphans. Fill us with your Spirit, and make us witnesses of hope. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: I will not leave you orphans
reflection.body:
After the death of Stephen, the Christians in Jerusalem are scattered, but the Gospel spreads with them. Philip goes to Samaria and proclaims Christ, and many are healed. "There was great joy in that city." When the apostles hear of it, they send Peter and John, who pray for the new believers and lay hands on them, "and they received the Holy Spirit." The Church has seen in this the roots of the sacrament of Confirmation.

In the Gospel, Jesus prepares his disciples for his departure. He links love and obedience: "If you love me, keep my commandments." And he makes a promise: "I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever: the Spirit of truth." The world cannot see the Spirit, but the disciples know him, "for he lives with you and will be in you."

Then Jesus speaks words of great tenderness: "I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you." Even after his Ascension, the disciples will not be alone. Through the Spirit, Jesus and the Father will live in them: "Because I live, you will live also."

Peter tells Christians how to live in a world that does not always understand them: "Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear." Our faith should be gentle, respectful and confident.

As Pentecost approaches, pray each day for the gift of the Holy Spirit. Think about how you would explain your hope to a friend who asked you why you believe. And if you know someone who feels abandoned, remind them by your presence that they are not orphans.
